Your smart home lighting lineup is probably mostly smaller bulbs and plug-in adapters, but the category is quickly maturing, and now full-sized hardwired fixtures are arriving with native Matter integration into Apple Home. SwitchBot recently launched its new SwitchBot RGBICWW Ceiling Light, bringing ultra-bright illumination and native Matter support directly to your overhead fixtures.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple’s smart home framework.

Native Matter and Apple Home integration

The biggest feature of this new ceiling light is out-of-the-box Matter support without needing a SwitchBot Hub. As long as your Apple TV 4K or HomePod is online, the fixture can connect directly to your existing ecosystem over a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.

Hardware size and brightness

SwitchBot offers two sizes to match different use cases. The 12-inch model targets hallways and bathrooms at 2,000 lumens. The larger 15-inch model fits living rooms and bedrooms at 3,200 lumens. SwitchBot has built-in smooth dimming from 100% down to 0%.

Most smart bulbs generally make you pick one color at a time. This light uses RGBIC technology with individual chips so it can show multiple colors on the ceiling at once for a dynamic lighting effect. If you prefer traditional lighting, it has dedicated warm white and cool white LEDs that can adjust color temperature from 2700K to 6500K. It also has power-off memory, so if you briefly lose power, the light will remember your previous brightness and color settings. I love this feature because every

SwitchBot RGBICWW review summary

Using 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi means adding another always-on device to your router on an older band. Thread radio would be ideal for snappy mesh responsiveness. But getting a hardwired, natively Matter-supported light for under $50 is a fantastic value for anyone looking to permanently upgrade their ceiling fixtures.

You can pick up the new Switchbot RGBICWW on Amazon.
